  PROBLEM: The `blocked_handoff` branch of the "Hand off CI-triage issue whose PR is no longer open" step has no marker-comment dedup. If the `ai:blocked` label write succeeds and the comment write fails, a retry posts a second identical `ai:implement-pr-not-open:v1` comment. The supersede branch already has this dedup.
  WHY: A retry after a partial failure yields duplicate informational marker comments. Routing is not broken, so the reviewer rated it NIT (mapped to low).
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:hand-off step (`${RUNTIME_DIR}` references for result_file, comments_file, comment_file) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The hand-off step references `${RUNTIME_DIR}` without a `:-` default, and the step `env:` block does not set it. With `set -u`, an unset value aborts the script early.
  WHY: An early abort leaves the issue in `ai:awaiting-approval` with no triage signal. The reviewer rated it NIT (mapped to low) because `RUNTIME_DIR` is set elsewhere in `implement.yml`.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:hand-off step `gh_retry` fallback (around line 690 of the patch) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `GH_API_RETRY_HELPERS` is unset, `gh_retry` falls back to a pass-through with no rate-limit classification or retry/backoff. The step does not bootstrap the helper the way the `Resolve integration ref` step does.
  WHY: A transient 403/429 on the hand-off path gets no retry, and rate-limit and budget tracking is under-reported. The reviewer rated it NIT (mapped to low) because the step makes only a few API calls.
